title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
summary:
Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock and have been suspended for the night, after running more than a day over time, as countries have been unable to agree on a new global climate deal.
The EU and Pacific island nations are amongst a group pushing back against the latest draft agreement which included no reference to reducing the world's demand for fossil fuels.
If countries cannot reach consensus - which is required by the UN's climate talks process - the negotiations could be suspended.
In that case the summit would end with no deal and be reconvened next year.
This has only happened once before since countries started holding COP climate meetings in 1995.

title: Fossil fuel talks deadlock pushes COP31 climate summit into overtime
summary:
EU warns COP31 risks turning into a ‘fossil summit’ as critical climate commitments are omitted from the draft deal.
The COP31 climate summit has gone into overtime as nearly 200 countries remain deadlocked over a draft deal that no longer mentions fossil fuels.
The fossil fuel fightAn opening draft from cohost and lead negotiator Australia on Monday called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels.
The European Union said the draft “risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit”.

title: COP31: New draft deal aims to avert collapse of talks at climate summit
summary:
Efforts to avert the collapse of talks at the UN COP31 summit have faced further delays on the second day of overtime, as countries struggle to reach a new global climate deal.
Countries were expected to reconvene to decide whether to approve a new deal, but that meeting was delayed on Sunday morning.
The president of the talks, Turkey's Environment Minister Murat Kurum, told the BBC he was "hopeful" of a breakthrough as he entered the summit on Sunday.
The EU and Pacific states had been arguing against the removal of fossil fuels from the draft text.
If countries cannot reach consensus - as required by the UN's climate talks process - the negotiations could be suspended until next year.

title: Making Earth Cool Again
summary:
Jayant Sinha A global AI ecosystem controlled by the US and China would make other countries dangerously dependent on foreign technologies.
Together, COP30’s global mobilization, negotiations, and Action Agenda revealed that the global climate regime is shifting from a negotiation track to a living system.
This implementation movement has allowed climate action to gain global scale, irrespective of backtracking by any specific country.
As the net-zero transition connects economies, societies, and governments at all levels through sustainable development, implementation coalitions increasingly cut across ideological and geopolitical lines, including entrenched North-South negotiating divides.
Looking ahead, our collective ambition must be to elevate climate solutions from niche applications to the mainstream.
